en: Taal Volcano in Batangas features a main crater lake situated on Volcano Island within Taal Lake.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Cagayan River in Luzon is the longest and largest river in the Philippines by water volume.
The Philippine eagle is a critically endangered bird endemic to the tropical forests of Mindanao and Luzon.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea protects over 600 species of diverse marine plants and animals.
Laguna de Bay in Luzon is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering roughly 900 square kilometers.
The Philippines produces most of the global supply of abaca, a strong plant fiber used for ropes.
The amihan is the cool northeast monsoon that brings dry weather to the Philippines between November and February.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park features an eight-kilometer underground river flowing directly into the sea.
Palawan is a long island province situated geographically between the South China Sea and the Sulu Sea.
Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for its perfectly symmetrical cone shape formed by repeated historical eruptions.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical limestone mounds that turn brown during summer.
